idiom_name: continuity struct + []Version sorted by time.Time with sort.Search as-of lookup
implementation_notes: Go models the roles as plain data: the continuity is a struct carrying the identity and a slice of Version structs ordered by their Effective time.Time, and the as-of lookup is sort.Search for the first version after the query date minus one - the temporal collection is just the sorted slice. Snapshots come free from value semantics (assigning a Version copies it), so the update path reads the current value, changes the copy and inserts it at its effective date, an ordinary insertion rather than an append-and-sort. There is no inheritance and no history framework to lean on, but the whole mechanism is a dozen lines of stdlib code, with slices.Insert (Go 1.21) performing the ordered insertion an amendment needs.
pitfalls: time.Time equality and ordering: == also compares the Location and the monotonic clock reading, so use Before/After/Equal (or Compare) and strip monotonic readings with Round(0); a time.Now() value and the same instant loaded from a database are not ==.
Monotonic readings make time.Time a poor map key and a poor cross-process comparison base: normalize to UTC at the boundary and store one location, and prefer a slice over a map keyed by time.Time.
A Terms value containing slices, maps or pointers is only shallowly copied, so a snapshot that shares a map with the previous version still mutates retroactively.
The insertion reuses the slice's backing array: two continuities must never share a versions slice, and code holding a previously returned []Version sees a shifted tail after an amendment.
